definition: A sworn legal document that every candidate must file when submitting their nomination. It declares the candidate's criminal record, financial assets, liabilities, and educational qualifications. Voters can access these affidavits on the ECI website.

Bharat Electronics Limited — one of only two government-owned companies authorized to manufacture Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and VVPAT units for Indian elections. BEL is headquartered in Bangalore.

A special election held to fill a single vacant seat in the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly. Vacancies arise due to the death, resignation, or disqualification of a sitting member. The ECI schedules by-elections within six months of a vacancy.

A defined geographic area that elects one representative to the Lok Sabha or State Assembly. India has 543 Lok Sabha constituencies. Constituency boundaries are determined by the Delimitation Commission.

The process of redrawing the boundaries of electoral constituencies to reflect changes in population. Delimitation is carried out by an independent Delimitation Commission, typically after a national census.
Electronics Corporation of India Limited — the second government-owned company authorized to manufacture EVMs and VVPAT machines. ECIL is headquartered in Hyderabad.

The Election Commission of India — an autonomous constitutional body responsible for administering all elections in India, including Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Assemblies, and the offices of President and Vice President.

Electoral Photo Identity Card, commonly known as the Voter ID card. Issued by the ECI, it serves as proof of identity at the polling booth. A digital version can be downloaded from the Voter Helpline app or the NVSP portal.

Electronic Voting Machine — a portable battery-operated device used to record votes in Indian elections. It replaced paper ballots starting from 1998 to reduce electoral fraud and speed up the counting process.

A survey conducted by media organizations or agencies immediately after voters leave the polling booth. Exit polls attempt to predict election results before official counting. They are banned from broadcast until the last phase of polling ends.

The official application form used to register as a new voter in India. Eligible citizens who are 18 or older can submit Form 6 online through the NVSP portal or the Voter Helpline app, along with proof of age and address.
The lower house of India's Parliament, also called the House of the People. It has 543 directly elected seats, with members elected through a first-past-the-post voting system for a 5-year term.

Model Code of Conduct — a set of guidelines issued by the ECI that all political parties and candidates must follow from the date elections are announced until results are declared. It ensures free and fair elections by restricting government announcements and campaigning.

None of the Above — an option on the EVM that allows voters to formally reject all candidates on the ballot. Introduced in 2013 following a Supreme Court directive, NOTA gives voters the right to express dissatisfaction without abstaining.

A representative appointed by a political party or candidate to be present inside the polling booth during voting. Polling agents observe the voting process to ensure fairness and can raise objections with the Presiding Officer.

A senior government official appointed by the ECI to manage a specific polling booth on election day. The Presiding Officer oversees the entire voting process, handles voter verification, manages the EVM, and ensures orderly conduct.
The upper house of India's Parliament, also called the Council of States. It has 245 members — 233 elected by State and UT assemblies, and 12 nominated by the President. Members serve 6-year terms.

A senior official responsible for conducting the entire election process in a single constituency. The RO oversees nomination filing, voter lists, polling arrangements, counting of votes, and the declaration of results.

A mandatory 48-hour campaign ban before polling day, as mandated by Section 126 of the Representation of the People Act 1951. During this period, all public meetings, processions, and media advertisements by parties are prohibited.

Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail — a printer-like device attached to EVMs that displays a paper slip showing the voter's selected candidate name and symbol for 7 seconds. The slip then drops into a sealed box for audit purposes.
